title: Limitation period - the silent killer of strong civil cases
p1:
A strong case can fail before it ever reaches the courtroom.

Not because the facts are weak. Not because the evidence is missing. But because time quietly ran out.
p2:
Many people believe that if they have a genuine legal claim, they can approach the court whenever they are ready. The surprising truth is that the law often puts a deadline on when a civil case can be filed.

This deadline is called the limitation period. Once it expires, even a deserving claim may become difficult or impossible to enforce.
p3:
For example, a person may have a valid dispute over money, property, or an agreement, but waiting too long to take action can weaken their legal position.

The lesson is simple: legal rights are not just about having a strong case. They are also about taking timely steps. Knowing the applicable deadline can protect a claim before it disappears silently.

A delayed action today can become a lost opportunity tomorrow.
conclusion: Have you ever seen a genuine claim become complicated because someone waited too long to take legal action?
